action: Universities: check whether admin, deployment and test pages are exposed externally, replace possibly stolen authentication keys and database accounts, and respond jointly with the vendor, as S2W advises.
date_note: Date of the Etnews article relaying S2W's report; the claimed intrusions were 12 to 17 November.
exec: A claimed campaign against Korean universities reportedly used an AI penetration-testing tool; the real scope is not confirmed.
plain: Security firm S2W says a hacker claimed to have breached Korean universities and posted data on Telegram, and that traces point to an AI-based attack tool. The real scope has not been confirmed.
summary: Etnews reports a hacker called KimJEN claimed to have hacked Korean universities and public bodies from 12 to 17 November, claiming about 100 universities; the actual scope is not confirmed. S2W found signs of an AI-based penetration-testing tool. Daily Secu interviewed a member of a team called KrrK who says student data was sold; the article reports no university confirmation and cannot confirm the KimJEN link.
title: S2W: hacker claims Korean university breaches using AI tool; scope unconfirmed

validation.note: Etnews (19 Nov, relaying S2W) and Dailysecu (24 Nov, interview with a KrrK member) read; both relay hacker claims; the S2W report and any university or vendor statement were not read.

review.note: tags claim, ai were not in the fixed list; set to ai-enabled. Claims, dates, S2W advice match Etnews and Dailysecu
